the command says in one line that the PATH link was skipped because the home is redirected, and prints the scratch binary\\u0027s path to call directly.\u0022,\u0022The same holds for h9k update under a redirected HALL9K_HOME, on macOS, Linux, and Windows (where the equivalent is the HKCU Environment\\\\Path append recorded in lesson 5082d6bc).\u0022,\u0022A default-home install still links onto the PATH exactly as today (retarget in place, never clobber a real file, fall back to ~/.local/bin), covered by the existing tests plus one new unit test over LinkOntoPath\\u0027s caller proving the redirected-home skip through a fake, with no real symlink or registry write.\u0022,\u0022docs/operations.md\\u0027s isolation paragraph (HALL9K_HOME) says what the redirect does and does not cover, and no longer needs the operator to restore a PATH link or registry entry by hand after a scratch run.\u0022],\u0022Type\u0022:\u0022Bugfix\u0022,\u0022AgentContext\u0022:\u0022Evidence (Mac, hall9k-3f, 2026-09-23 11:06 EDT, while running the macOS half of 9d30a92a\\u0027s criterion 1 with the card\\u0027s recipe): the scratch run\\u0027s own stdout printed \\u0027On PATH: /Users/brianhallmanac/.local/bin/h9k -\\u003E /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/home42/bin/h9k\\u0027, so the v0.10.45 h9k running under HALL9K_HOME=\\u003Cscratch\\u003E retargeted the operator\\u0027s real PATH link at the scratch bin. When the scratch tree was deleted the link dangled and every h9k call in the orchestrator window failed with \\u0027command not found\\u0027 until the live h9k update --restart to v0.10.45 at 11:36 EDT re-pointed it (its output: \\u0027On PATH: /Users/brianhallmanac/.local/bin/h9k -\\u003E /Users/brianhallmanac/.hall9k/bin/h9k\\u0027). Source: InstallCommand.LinkOntoPath / LinkSomewhere (src/Hall9k.Cli/Commands/InstallCommand.cs around line 1893) walks the PATH and retargets any existing h9k link in place; nothing in that path consults PlatformPaths.Home or HALL9K_HOME. The Windows build session of 9d30a92a hit the same class on its side (the install appends its bin directory to the HKCU Environment\\\\Path; snapshot and restore it) and recorded it as lesson 5082d6bc; this task is the fix for both halves, not a new lesson. Reproduction: HALL9K_HOME=\\u003Cscratch\\u003E HALL9K_CONNECTION_STRING=\\u003Cscratch db\\u003E \\u003Cscratch\\u003E/bin/h9k install --from-release \\u003Cextracted payload\\u003E --now (with --restart and a dummy pid if you want the restart too); then ls -l ~/.local/bin/h9k. Never run this against the live home. Related: 9d30a92a (Done, the recipe\\u0027s origin), lesson 5082d6bc, assembly rule a907b770. the resolved platform home is not the default ~/.hall9k (HALL9K_HOME set to another directory), h9k install --from-release \\u003Cpayload\\u003E neither creates nor retargets an h9k link in any PATH directory, /opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin, or ~/.local/bin; it prints one line saying the PATH link was skipped because the home is redirected, together with the scratch binary\\u0027s full path to call directly.\u0022,\u0022The same holds for h9k update under a redirected home on macOS, Linux, and Windows: on Windows the guard sits in front of the HKCU Environment\\\\Path prepend (lesson 5082d6bc) and the skip line names the bin directory; on every platform the skip line also says to add it to PATH by hand if this relocated install is meant to be permanent.\u0022,\u0022A default-home install links onto the PATH exactly as today (retarget in place, never clobber a real file, fall back to ~/.local/bin, prepend on Windows), covered by the existing tests; the skip decision is a single question on the platform-paths helper (is the home redirected), and one new unit test sets the test-only home override to a scratch path and proves the finish step skips both the symlink branch and the registry branch, with no real symlink, registry write, or process environment change.\u0022,\u0022docs/operations.md gains a short paragraph beneath the HALL9K_HOME row of its environment table (no isolation paragraph exists today) saying that a redirected home relocates everything on disk and skips the PATH link, so a scratch run under it never touches the live h9k command, and that a permanently relocated install adds its bin directory to PATH by hand.\u0022]},\u0022AgentContext\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022BlockedBy\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022Type\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022Model\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022RevisedAt\u0022:\u00222026-09-24T19:04:14.808026\u002B00:00\u0022,\u0022RevisedByOwnerId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5a50-7368-b048-72bcfee948bf\u0022,\u0022EpicId\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022QueuePriority\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022ReviewStageComposition\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022ReviewStageCompositionAcknowledged\u0022:false,\u0022ClearInteractiveMode\u0022:false,\u0022StackedOnTaskId\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022StackedOnPullRequestNumber\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022CloseLinkedIssue\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022SpikeKind\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022ExitCriterion\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022Constraints\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false}}","originEventId":"854646db-74c6-4aa6-9fb0-b5d41b64c9fd","originSequence":63528,"originNodeId":"01a00d41-5b80-753d-a3f1-070b25e490e4","originOwnerRootFingerprint":"c8f5c85900dac9911ce1ada43484dc7bf91a2a3e86efa8812d9f84cfd25bf2ac","originAt":"2026-09-24T19:04:14.821458+00:00","originProjectId":"01a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71"},{"streamId":"01a0ceea-653f-724c-8995-570aa50ce8e3","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Tasks.Events.TaskRevised","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a0ceea-653f-724c-8995-570aa50ce8e3\u0022,\u0022Objective\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:[\u0022When the resolved platform home is not the default (\\u003CUserProfile\\u003E/.hall9k, compared as full paths with the trailing separator ignored and case ignored on Windows; HALL9K_HOME naming exactly the default is not a redirect), h9k install (--repo and --from-release alike) and h9k update neither create nor retarget an h9k link in any PATH directory, /opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin, or ~/.local/bin, and on Windows neither read nor write HKCU\\\\Environment\\\\Path; instead they print one line saying the PATH link was skipped because the home is redirected, naming \\u003Chome\\u003E/bin/h9k (the bin directory on Windows), and saying to add it to PATH by hand if the relocation is permanent.\u0022,\u0022The decision is one question on PlatformPaths (is the home redirected), computed from the same resolution Home uses so the test-only override counts, and asked once in InstallCommand.FinishAsync ahead of the operating-system switch so the symlink branch and the registry branch both sit under it; LinkOntoPath, EnsureOnWindowsPath, and UninstallCommand are unchanged.\u0022,\u0022A default-home install links exactly as today (retarget in place, never clobber a real file, fall back to ~/.local/bin, prepend on Windows), covered by the existing tests. FinishAsync takes the PATH value and the profile directory as optional parameters defaulting to today\\u0027s environment reads; one new test under the scoped test home calls FinishAsync with linking on, an empty PATH, and a temporary profile, and proves the skip line is printed and no link exists under that profile, so a regression can only ever write inside the temporary directory; a second, pure test covers the comparison for the exact default, a trailing separator, a relative path, and case on Windows. No test sets a process environment variable or touches the registry; the CI Windows leg is what executes the registry side of the gate.\u0022,\u0022docs/operations.md gains a sentence or short paragraph beneath the HALL9K_HOME row of its environment table saying that a redirected home relocates everything on disk and skips the PATH link, so a scratch run under it never touches the live h9k, and that a permanently relocated install adds its bin directory to PATH by hand; no other document changes.\u0022]},\u0022AgentContext\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:\u0022Evidence (Mac, hall9k-3f, 2026-09-23 11:06 EDT, while running the macOS half of 9d30a92a\\u0027s criterion 1 with the card\\u0027s recipe): the scratch run\\u0027s own stdout printed \\u0027On PATH: /Users/brianhallmanac/.local/bin/h9k -\\u003E /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/home42/bin/h9k\\u0027, so the v0.10.45 h9k running under HALL9K_HOME=\\u003Cscratch\\u003E retargeted the operator\\u0027s real PATH link at the scratch bin. When the scratch tree was deleted the link dangled and every h9k call in the orchestrator window failed with \\u0027command not found\\u0027 until the live h9k update --restart to v0.10.45 at 11:36 EDT re-pointed it. Windows hit the same class on its side (the install prepends its bin directory to HKCU Environment\\\\Path) and recorded it as lesson 5082d6bc in the project home\\u0027s lessons.md; this task fixes both halves.\\n\\nWhere the code is (main at cf39b90ba, v0.10.46): InstallCommand.FinishAsync (line 180, bool linkOntoPath = true; the gate goes at line 324 ahead of the OperatingSystem.IsWindows() switch, whose two arms are EnsureOnWindowsPath at line 328 and LinkOntoPath at line 332 with the PATH and user-profile reads at lines 334 and 335); LinkOntoPath at line 1941 and EnsureOnWindowsPath at line 783 have no other production caller, FinishAsync\\u0027s only callers are InstallCommand.ExecuteAsync line 145 and UpdateCommand.RunAsync line 186, and every test caller passes linkOntoPath: false (UpdateCommandTests lines 25 to 33 record why: an early test wiped the real PATH). PlatformPaths.Home (src/Hall9k.Domain/Infrastructure/Storage/PlatformPaths.cs line 21) resolves HomeOverrideForTests (an AsyncLocal), then HALL9K_HOME, then \\u003CUserProfile\\u003E/.hall9k; the link target is always \\u003Chome\\u003E/bin/h9k because DaemonRuntime.BinDirectory is RunPaths.Root/bin and RunPaths.Root is PlatformPaths.Home (RunPaths.cs line 25). The bootstrap scripts hand off to h9k install --from-release and link nothing; DaemonRestartHandoff spawns only daemon stop and daemon start; UninstallCommand (lines 591 and 651) removes only a link resolving to exactly \\u003Chome\\u003E/bin/h9k and only its own bin directory from the registry PATH, so it is already safe and stays unchanged. Comparison shape: Path.GetFullPath both sides, trailing separator trimmed, OrdinalIgnoreCase on Windows and Ordinal elsewhere; a relative HALL9K_HOME resolves against the working directory like every other reader; a symlinked default home reads as redirected and the message covers it. Message text names the path neutrally, since under a permanent relocation the binary is not scratch: \\u0027PATH link skipped: the home is redirected to X; call X/bin/h9k directly, or add X/bin to your PATH if this relocation is permanent\\u0027. Fold-in only if already in the file: scripts/install.ps1 line 141 prints \\u0027Done. Open a new terminal so h9k resolves on your PATH\\u0027 unconditionally, false after a skip; install.sh already branches on command -v h9k. Do not add a --no-link-path flag (parked until a real operator relocates permanently). Walked with Brian 2026-09-24 and challenged by a headless session the same afternoon (verdict in this task\\u0027s journal.md); Brian accepted the verdict\\u0027s criteria and calls.\\n\\nNotes to the orchestrator, not for the build session to act on: at closeout, lesson 5082d6bc\\u0027s first clause (snapshot and restore the Windows user PATH around a scratch run) is superseded by this fix and its second clause (a real h9kd against the scratch store is a real daemon) stands; record that in lessons.md.
